title: Conditional Residence Times and Sequential Transition Dynamics of an Overdamped Dimere
abstract: We investigate the completion dynamics of an overdamped dimer moving in a bistable potential under thermal fluctuations and a weak periodic force. Both monomers start in one of the two wells separated by a barrier. The transition is initiated when the monomer closer to the barrier makes a jump across it. The completion dynamics refers to the next part of the dynamics where the second monomer has to wait for some time before it can follow up. We use the Conditional Residence Time (CRT) to study the delay between the successive barrier crossing of the two monomers. The CRT distributions highlight qualitatively different regimes formed by the competition between the escape times of the lagging monomer and the time period of the external drive. The effect is strongest in the weak coupling regime where the delayed completion is spread across multiple forcing cycles. By partitioning this process into three windows, i.e. the immediate, first cycle and later cycles, we show that the probability that the lagging monomer will make a transition in the said cycle is redistributed among these pathways as we change the frequency of the drive. This leads to a non-monotonic dependence of the mean CRT on the frequency of the drive. Our results demonstrate that transition initiation and completion in a coupled system are two separate processes and establish CRT as a useful measure to quantify the sequential barrier crossing dynamics in coupled stochastic systems.
summary: This work analyzes how two coupled particles (a dimer) transition across a barrier under external periodic driving and thermal noise. By introducing the Conditional Residence Time (CRT), the authors show that the time delay between the two monomers crossing the barrier is highly sensitive to the drive frequency. This establishes CRT as a key measure for understanding sequential, rate-limiting steps in coupled stochastic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the completion dynamics of an overdamped dimer moving in a bistable potential under thermal fluctuations and a weak periodic force.
main_result: The mean Conditional Residence Time (CRT) exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the external drive frequency, demonstrating that transition initiation and completion are distinct sequential processes.
method: The authors use the Conditional Residence Time (CRT) as a diagnostic tool to quantify the delay between successive barrier crossings of two coupled monomers.
model_or_system: The system is an overdamped dimer modeled by coupled Langevin equations in a one-dimensional double well potential, incorporating harmonic and Lennard-Jones interactions, thermal noise, and a weak sinusoidal external force.
key_observables: Conditional Residence Time (CRT), Mean First Passage Times (MFPTs), Escape rates, Probability distributions of transition windows.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($k$), external drive frequency ($\Omega$), Noise strength ($D$), and the competition between escape times and the driving period.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the process can be partitioned into distinct time windows (immediate, first cycle, later cycles) to analyze sequential dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate CRT distributions for varying coupling strengths and drive frequencies, showing how the mean CRT changes non-monotonically with $\Omega$, especially in the weak coupling regime.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical model and Langevin equations, defines the CRT diagnostic tool, analyzes the dynamics by partitioning the process into three time windows, and concludes by establishing CRT's utility for sequential barrier crossing analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on classical stochastic dynamics, the concept of analyzing sequential transitions (initiation vs. completion) using a specialized time delay metric like CRT is highly relevant to understanding decoherence or multi-step quantum tunneling processes in open quantum systems.
